cases.clinical_note: SYNTHETIC CASE. Patient: Alex Patel, age 52. Visit dates: 2026-03-02, 2026-04-10, 2026-05-18. History: persistent low back pain for 4 months, with prior visits for back pain and leg symptoms. Exam shows radicular pain with motor weakness in the L5 distribution and diminished Achilles reflex. The patient completed 6 weeks of conservative therapy with moderate activity, analgesics, NSAIDs, and muscle relaxants, with no improvement after 6 weeks of conservative therapy. Imaging requested: lumbar spine MRI. Prior therapy: moderate activity, analgesics, NSAIDs, and muscle relaxants as tolerated.

SYNTHETIC CASE. Patient: Alex Kim, age 48. Visit dates: 2026-02-14, 2026-03-20, 2026-04-28. History: knee pain for 5 months, worse with stairs and prolonged standing. Patient reports significant knee pain with mechanical symptoms, including knee locking and catching in the knee. Imaging grade is Kellgren-Lawrence grade 2, consistent with mild osteoarthritis. MRI shows meniscal tear in the medial meniscus. The patient completed 6 weeks of formal physical therapy in the past year, confirmed by PT notes. Imaging requested: knee arthroscopy with possible partial meniscectomy.

SYNTHETIC CASE. Patient: Jordan Nguyen, age 34. Visit dates: 2026-01-12, 2026-02-09, 2026-03-16. History: abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss over 8 months, with prior gastroenterology follow-up. Infliximab was prescribed by a gastroenterologist. Diagnosis is moderate to severe Crohn disease. Planned dosing is 5 mg per kg at weeks 0, 2, and 6, then maintenance dosing every 6 weeks. TB screening documented before initiation, with a negative result. The patient failed corticosteroids and failed immunomodulators, with documented intolerance to prior therapy. Treatment requested: infliximab intravenous infusion.
